clue.text: Head leaving Bedfordshire town is not settled

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, and leaving says that letter departs

parts.note: Dunstable is a market town in the English county of Bedfordshire

explanation.surface: A school principal who is moving away from a town in Bedfordshire has yet to find a home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head leaving' removes the first letter, D, from Dunstable, a town in the English county of Bedfordshire. The head looks like a head teacher but is only the front of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something shaky or liable to change has not come to rest.

clue.text: Style any MP "a real runt" and one could be this

indicators.note: to style something is to fashion or shape it, so the letters that follow are refashioned

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Call a Member of Parliament a pathetic little weakling and you would be breaking the rules of the House.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Style' is the anagram indicator, working on ANY MP, A REAL RUNT and I (one). The whole clue also describes the answer: insulting language of this kind is ruled out of order in the House of Commons.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: insulting a fellow member in the Commons is language the Speaker rules out of order, which is what the pronoun points to.

clue.text: Stupid person is raising a protest

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising the words before it makes them read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: nit is British slang for a foolish person
taken as written

explanation.surface: Some fool is getting a demonstration going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' turns NIT IS upside down in this down entry. Nit is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: occupying a place and refusing to move is one form of demonstration.

clue.text: Overhead for small supermarket better than expected

parts.note: something overhead is above you

indicators.note: small says the shop's name is made smaller, losing its opening letter, which is also the usual abbreviation of small

parts.note: Spar is a chain of convenience supermarkets common in Britain and Europe

explanation.surface: The running costs of a little grocery shop turned out more favourable than forecast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small' cuts the S from SPAR, a chain of convenience shops common in Britain. 'Overhead' looks like a business cost but simply means higher up.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a result that beats the normal standard exceeds what was forecast.

clue.text: Ring up about one purple shrub

indicators.note: about puts the word for ring around the letter for one
in a down clue, up makes the assembled letters read from the bottom to the top

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Someone phones to ask about a single violet-coloured bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps CALL round I to give CALIL, and 'up' turns that upside down in this down entry. 'Ring up' reads as one phrase but is two instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a garden bush known for its mauve, scented flowers.

clue.text: Expanding bullet for which abuse is repeatedly rejected

indicators.note: repeatedly says the turned-back word is written twice over
rejected means sent back, so the word for abuse is written backwards

parts.note: mud is abuse or slander, as in mud-slinging

explanation.surface: A kind of ammunition whose misuse is turned down again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' sends MUD back to give DUM, and 'repeatedly' writes it twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a soft-nosed round designed to spread out on impact.

clue.text: U-turn Maggie finally contrived? Not so

indicators.note: contrived means artfully worked out, so the letters of the phrase before it are worked into a new order
finally takes the last letter of the name it follows

explanation.surface: Did Margaret Thatcher engineer a change of policy in the end? No, that is false.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrived' rearranges UTURN into UNTRU, and 'finally' adds the last letter of Maggie. The surface recalls Margaret Thatcher's line that 'the lady's not for turning'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something false is not the case.

clue.text: Trouble in a desperate condition endlessly upset eastern leader

indicators.note: in places the word for trouble inside the letters built from the rest of the wordplay
in a down clue, upset overturns the letters so they read from the bottom up
endlessly removes the last letter of the word for a condition

parts.note: a malady is a serious illness or disorder
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Strife during a hopeless and unending crisis unsettled a ruler in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops a Y, 'upset' turns AMALAD into DALAMA in this down entry, and 'in' then opens that up. The surface suggests a crisis, hiding the Tibetan spiritual figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the spiritual head of Tibetan Buddhism is a figure of authority in Asia.

clue.text: Model did many a service? She would, wouldn't she!

indicators.note: to model is to shape or mould, so the letters that follow are moulded into a new form

explanation.surface: A showgirl performed plenty of favours, and of course she was bound to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' is the anagram indicator. She was a model in Britain's 1963 Profumo scandal, famous for saying in court 'He would, wouldn't he?' when told a lord denied knowing her; the definition twists that line.
explanation.definitionFit: Allusion: the showgirl of the Profumo affair is remembered for her courtroom quip, here turned back on herself.

clue.text: Korean, for example, appears in London soccer team, one on top of league

parts.note: Leyton Orient is a football club in east London, often just called Orient
one can be the indefinite article, a

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A footballer from Seoul turns out for a club in the capital that sits first in the table.
explanation.walkthrough: ORIENT is Leyton Orient, a football club in east London. 'top of' takes the first letter of league.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a person from Korea comes from East Asia.

clue.text: Kitty, beginner in bakery can work to deliver bread fast

parts.note: the kitty is the pot of money in a card game

indicators.note: the beginner in a word is its first letter

parts.note: an oiler is an oil can with a long spout

explanation.surface: A trainee at the baker's named Kitty is able to labour so the loaves go out quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginner in' takes the first letter of bakery. The definition is the trap: bread is slang for money, so this is a book or film knocked out quickly to earn some.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a hasty book or film made only to bring in money, bread being slang for cash.

clue.text: Some went along with cards left after deal

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few players carried on the game holding whatever remained once the hands were given out.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft definition began at 'with', but the answer is a noun for the undealt stock, so 'with' is only a link and the definition starts at 'cards'. 'Some' marks the run inside 'went along'.
explanation.definitionFit: Technical term: in card games the undealt stock remaining on the table has this name.

clue.text: Short of capital, mobile phone company cover a certain area

indicators.note: a word's capital is its opening letter, and being short of it means that letter is missing

parts.note: Orange was a major British and French mobile phone network

explanation.surface: Lacking funds, a telecoms firm can only provide signal in one particular region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short of capital' removes the first letter of ORANGE, formerly one of Britain's main mobile phone networks. Capital looks like money but means the opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to roam or extend over a stretch of territory.

clue.text: Fool lured in London, say, showing naivety

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged letters inside the word for a place such as London

parts.note: London is an example of a city

indicators.note: to fool with something is to tamper with it, so the letters of the next word are tampered with

explanation.surface: A simpleton enticed into the capital shows how gullible he is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fool' looks like the victim of the story but is the anagram indicator, giving REDUL, which 'in' then encloses. 'London, say' asks for the kind of place London is, not a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both mean a readiness to believe things too easily, or gullibility.

clue.text: I note game needing a court (enclosed as shown here)

parts.note: NB, nota bene, is the abbreviation meaning note well
rackets is a fast ball game played in an enclosed court, a forerunner of squash

explanation.surface: Someone observes that a sport cannot be played without a proper court, adding a remark in parentheses.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points at itself: the clue's last words are printed inside parentheses, which shows how they are enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-reference: the words are printed between parentheses, the punctuation marks the phrase names.

clue.text: In SW London district, one's accompanied by singers

indicators.note: In says the letters that follow sit inside the name of the district

parts.note: Barnes is a riverside district of south-west London
the Roman numeral for one is I
to means accompanied by, as in singing to a piano

explanation.surface: In a corner of south-west London, a person has vocalists for company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like scene-setting but is the container signal. 'accompanied by' is the small word used in 'singing to a guitar'; the district is a riverside one by the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: men with voices between tenor and bass are one kind of vocalist.

clue.text: Look up a bird and carry on

indicators.note: in a down clue, up makes the word for look read from the bottom to the top

parts.note: to peek is to take a quick look
a tit is a small songbird such as the blue tit

explanation.surface: Find a species in the field guide and then continue birdwatching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns PEEK upside down in this down entry. 'Look up' reads as consulting a book but is two separate instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: an encouragement to persevere with what you are doing.

clue.text: What c clay became in part of Africa …

parts.note: the boxer Cassius Clay changed his name to Muhammad, so the initial C became this initial
the boxer Cassius Clay took this new surname in 1964

explanation.surface: Wondering what a certain kind of clay turned into somewhere on the African continent.
explanation.walkthrough: The boxer Cassius Clay became Muhammad Ali, so C Clay, written the same way with initial and surname, became these letters. Clay looks like earth but is the man.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a landlocked West African country is one region of that continent.

clue.text: Head inspires a right row in public school arrangement

indicators.note: to inspire is to breathe in, so the word for head takes the following letters inside it

parts.note: the head is a ship's toilet, and bog is British slang for a toilet
a row, rhymed with cow, is a noisy din

explanation.surface: A headmaster provokes a proper argument at a fee-paying school over how things are organised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspires' means breathes in: BOG, British slang for a toilet as head is naval slang for one, takes in A, R and DIN. In Britain a public school is a fee-paying one, where pupils often live in.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: living at school during term is the usual set-up at Britain's fee-paying independent schools.

clue.text: … The greatest! About right for a natural comedian

indicators.note: About puts the word for the greatest around the letter for right

parts.note: max, short for maximum, is the greatest amount

explanation.surface: Continuing from the boxer: he was the best, and also just the man to be a born funny man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' wraps MAX round R. The ellipsis ties 'The greatest' to the boxer of the previous clue, but here it only means the maximum; the comedian is Groucho or one of his brothers.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Groucho, Harpo and Chico, sharing this surname, were born funny men of film.

clue.text: Distribute again in proper place

parts.note: proper means real or genuine, as in a proper job
to place something is to locate it

explanation.surface: Hand things out once more, this time to the correct spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'place' looks like a noun but is the verb to locate.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to share out resources afresh, assigning them differently.

clue.text: Sounds like ecstasy reduced for a tenant

indicators.note: Sounds like says the phrase that follows is heard, not read

parts.note: E is slang for the drug, and a smaller dose of it is a two-word spoken phrase: a comparative meaning not so much, then the drug's letter

explanation.surface: It seems the renter is being given a smaller supply of the party drug.
explanation.walkthrough: E is slang for the drug ecstasy. Say the phrase for a smaller dose of it, and 'Sounds like' turns that into the word for someone holding a lease.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a person who holds a lease on a property rents it.

clue.text: Little time to go, fancy Tate modern or a cathedral?

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or ornamented, so the remaining letters are elaborately rearranged
to go says the letter for time departs from the gallery's name

parts.note: T is the abbreviation, the little form, of time

explanation.surface: With only a few minutes left on a sightseeing trip, would you like an art gallery or a great church?
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go' removes one T from TATE MODERN, and 'fancy' is the anagram indicator for the letters left. Fancy looks like a verb asking what you would like.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the great Gothic church on an island in the Seine in Paris.

clue.text: Extract from English and Italian leader

parts.note: Il Duce, the leader, was the title of the Italian dictator Mussolini

explanation.surface: A passage taken from the writings of an Englishman and a head of the Italian government.
explanation.walkthrough: Extract looks like a noun, a passage from a text, but is the verb to draw out. DUCE was Mussolini's title.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to draw out or bring forth something latent.

clue.text: Get a drink and book a dance

parts.note: rum is a spirit, an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Buy yourself something at the bar and reserve a turn on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'book' looks like the verb to reserve but is the noun, abbreviated to B.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a rhythmic ballroom style that came from Cuba.

clue.text: Note friend from Paris is in us city

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
ami is the French word for friend, as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: Mark it down: a French pal has turned up in an American town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from Paris' asks for the French word for friend. Note looks like a verb but is a note of the scale.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the resort and port in Florida is an American metropolis.

clue.text: Scandinavian singer is a long time going round Norway

indicators.note: going round wraps the word for a long time around the letter for Norway

parts.note: ages means a very long time, as in waiting for ages
N is the international vehicle registration code for Norway

explanation.surface: A Nordic vocalist spends years touring one of the countries there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' wraps AGES about N. The singer is the Swedish pop star known by her first name alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Swedish pop star Carlsson, who performs under her first name, is a Nordic vocalist.

clue.text: Rattle put in air associated with one Bellini opera

indicators.note: to rattle something is to shake it about, so the letters that follow are shaken up

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: The conductor Simon Rattle adds a tune linked to a particular work for the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rattle' is the anagram indicator, turning PUT IN AIR into the first eight letters. It looks like the conductor Sir Simon Rattle, which suits the musical surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the composer's last stage work, about Roundheads and Cavaliers in the English Civil War.

clue.text: Middle east country housing is for regime sycophants

indicators.note: housing says the country's name has the letter for is living inside it

parts.note: Yemen is a country at the southern end of the Arabian peninsula
is contracts to 's, as in he's, giving the letter S

explanation.surface: In an Arab state, homes are reserved for the government's flatterers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'housing' places S, the contracted form of is, inside YEMEN. Housing looks like a noun for homes but is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: people who agree with everything those in power say are flatterers.

clue.text: Writer using wrong books

parts.note: a pen is a thing that writes

indicators.note: wrong says the letters of the word before it are out of their proper order

explanation.surface: An author is consulting the incorrect volumes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' is the anagram indicator, turning USING into GUINS. The answer is the familiar name for paperbacks from a famous British publisher with a bird as its logo.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: paperbacks from the British publisher with the flightless bird logo are known by this name.
